thread.title: Trade uncertainty is the top factor that could determine the market's direction

author: Scott Gamm
title: Trade uncertainty is the top factor that could determine the market's direction
text: President Donald Trump listens during a meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron during the G-7 summit, Friday, June 8, 2018, in Charlevoix, Canada. (AP Photo/Evan Vucci) More Forget the Federal Reserve — President Trump’s trade policies should shape your investing strategy in 2019. That’s the assessment from JJ Kinahan, TD Ameritrade’s chief market strategist. The markets could get a dose of clarity on trade following Trump’s closely watched meeting with China’s President Xi Jinping at this week’s G-20 Summit in Argentina. Still, it’s up to Trump on whether to proceed with tariff increases against Chinese goods that are set to take effect in early January. “Every time we talk about tariffs, the market moves big one way or the other,” Kinahan told Yahoo Finance. “When the Fed speaks, you see a minor reaction overall — That tells you exactly where the market’s focus is right now.” Though investors remain worried about multiple rate hikes planned for 2019, Kinahan is laser focused on trade. “Much of [2019’s market outlook] is going to depend on where we end up with tariffs,” he said. The tech sector If a deal is reached between the U.S. and China and the tariff increases don’t take effect, Kinahan thinks the technology sector will lead the market. “Tech has suffered the most: the chipmakers, Apple (AAPL) and its suppliers,” he said. On Monday, Trump referenced the possibility of tariffs on Apple’s iPhone and laptops in an interview with The Wall Street Journal, sending Apple deeper into bear market territory on Tuesday. Apple shares are down 25.4% form their closing high of $232.07 a share on Oct. 3. Chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ), widely viewed as a bellwether for the technology sector, saw its shares slump about 47% from its closing high of $289.36 on Oct. 1. The Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) is down almost 13% from its Aug. 29 high of roughly 8,109. The financials sector However, if the 25% tariffs against hundreds of billions of dollars of Chinese goods do take effect, Kinahan sees opportunity within the financials sector. “They’ve been the most frustrating investment for people in 2018 — interest rates are rising, but the bank stocks haven’t moved,” he said, referring to the positive correlation between interest rate hikes and bank profit margins. The S&P 500 financials sector is down 5.3% since the start of the year. Goldman Sachs ( GS ) shares are down roughly 28% from its Jan. 30 high of $268.94. Kinahan sees upside in the big banks but also some of the mid-sized domestic banks that are part of the Russell 2000, as investors may flock toward companies with big domestic businesses in the face of tariffs.
